clue.text: Father and British girl love framing old picture for artist

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: framing means the girl-and-love pair is placed around the next two pieces like a frame around a picture

parts.note: a lass is a girl
pic is short for picture
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A family scene: dad and a British girlfriend pose for an old picture painted by some artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' and 'girl' join as one container that wraps around 'old picture', the two pieces after it in the clue; 'love' is the tennis score nil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism is perhaps the most famous artist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Break for driver in worst possible place on summit

parts.note: the pits is slang for the very worst place or thing
the top is the summit of a hill

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls over to rest in a dreadful spot right at the top of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a driver halts briefly in the pits for fuel and tyres, a short pause in the race.

clue.text: Keep it in mind as island home for us

indicators.note: in tells us the word it is placed within the word for mind

parts.note: the brain is the seat of the mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to remember something, followed by a patriotic nod to the island where we live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep it in mind' reads as an instruction to remember. The definition assumes the British setter and readership of the Daily Telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is the large island on which the newspaper's British readers live.

clue.text: Pollution produced by paints — small amounts

parts.note: oils are oil paints, as used by artists
a lick of paint is a small amount of it

explanation.surface: An environmental complaint that a little paint here and there is polluting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilled crude oil spreading over the sea is a classic form of marine pollution.

clue.text: South American people put into container? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: in case describes something placed inside a box or holder

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about packing South Americans away in a box, with a doubting afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: IN CASE loses its final E to leave the people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled much of the Andes in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: In nasa lab, amazing state of some Americans

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a NASA laboratory located in a southern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'nasALAB, AMAzing'; 'amazing' looks like praise but just supplies the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty United States, home to some Americans.

clue.text: Singer taking offence at artist

parts.note: a sin is an offence against moral law
taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A vocalist gets upset by something a painter has done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking offence' looks like one idea, being upset; here 'taking' is just a link and 'offence' gives SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American crooner of the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: As artist, Elton is superior to bobby

indicators.note: in a down clue being superior means sitting above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: Elton John is the British pop star
a bobby is British slang for a police officer, whose basic rank is constable

explanation.surface: A claim that the singer Elton outranks a policeman when it comes to art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' reads as better; in a down entry it means placed higher. A BOBBY is a British police officer, named after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was the English Romantic landscape painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: German master mishandled the three rs? Bad clue!

indicators.note: mishandled shows the letters are roughly treated and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
three Rs read literally as the letter R three times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that an old master made a mess of the three Rs of schooling, followed by a solver's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the three Rs' suggests reading, writing and arithmetic, but it is just RRR; with THE and BADCLUE that makes thirteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer of Nuremberg was a master painter and engraver of the German Renaissance.

clue.text: Cricket side before test being judged

indicators.note: before places the cricket piece ahead of the test piece

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A cricket team turns up ahead of a Test match, waiting to be assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test' tempts a cricket Test match; it is just TRIAL. In cricket, the ON side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant in court is under trial, with a verdict pending.

clue.text: Course that's seen on TV

definitions.meaning: a course in the sense of a passage or route for water, a watercourse
a television station broadcasting its programmes

explanation.surface: A remark about a series of lessons being broadcast on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a waterway's route and a broadcasting station you tune into.

clue.text: A couple of things needed for tennis or another sport

parts.words: A couple of things needed for tennis
parts.note: two items any tennis game requires: the mesh across the court and the thing hit over it

parts.words: A couple of things needed for tennis
parts.note: two items any tennis game requires: the mesh across the court and the thing hit over it

explanation.surface: A list of equipment for tennis, or perhaps for some other game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' warns that the sport is not tennis but a different one using the same two items.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, mainly played by women, in which players shoot a ball through a raised hoop.

clue.text: Broadcast improvisational jazz singer?

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to sow or spread widely, as seed is cast
someone who scats, singing wordless syllables in jazz, playfully named with an -er ending

explanation.surface: A radio show features a jazz vocalist who makes it up as they go along.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: one who scats.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow seed widely by hand is to strew it far and wide; a scat singer improvises nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Plant represented in gold brooch

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a pin is a brooch or ornamental clasp

explanation.surface: A flower design rendered in a golden piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented in' is a link joining the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a succulent stonecrop, and orpin is an older spelling of that same herb's name.

clue.text: Coach and horse in near-accident

indicators.note: in places the horse within the shortened word for accident
near means almost, so the word falls one letter short of whole

parts.note: chance is luck or accident
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A coach and a horse are almost involved in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near-accident' looks like a narrow escape; 'near' trims the last letter, leaving CHANC to hold the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Attacker using wild alsatians

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run loose and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets ferocious guard dogs on a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: An ALSATIAN is the British name for a German shepherd dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is one who assaults or attacks someone.

clue.text: Put name on lots of letters for travel guides

parts.note: to sign is to write your name on something
the posts are the deliveries of mail, many letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to write your name on a heap of postcards when touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' tempts the alphabet; here it is mail, the POSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadside signs pointing the way guide travellers to their destinations.

clue.text: Relative support for one on course, recipient of funding

parts.note: gran, a grandmother, is a relative
a tee is the peg holding up a golf ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: A family member backs a student on a course and receives money for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one on course' suggests a student; it is a golf ball, held up by a TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: One given a grant, such as a research award, is a person who receives funding.

clue.text: Rope in one of those marginalised here, say

definitions.meaning: a rope at the bow of a boat used to tie it up

definitions.text: one of those marginalised here, say
definitions.meaning: one of the artists whose names sit around the edges of this grid

explanation.surface: A rope is used to haul in one of the people pushed to society's edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The four outer entries of the grid are all artists, literally on its margins, so 'marginalised here' points to an example of them.
explanation.definitionFit: On a boat a mooring line at the bow has this name; the edge entries name artists who make pictures.

clue.text: Space traveller needs to arrive ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the arriving word before the time letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: An astronaut must turn up early.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body that journeys through the solar system on a long orbit.

clue.text: Leading players, as actor's involved with a second

indicators.note: involved in the sense of tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Stars of a show, since one performer is working alongside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a second' looks like a second actor; it is just S, set after the rearranged letters of 'actor's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-stars share the top billing, as joint leading performers.

clue.text: Girl and European joined dance centre in spring

parts.note: May is a girl's name
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A young woman and a continental partner take up dancing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' refers to May Day celebrations, when villagers in England dance round a ribboned pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbon dances circle a tall pole on village greens on May Day, so it stands at their centre.

clue.text: A king gripped by a sin — greed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: gripped by means the king pair is held inside the sin word

parts.note: a vice is a sin or moral failing
taken as written
R, from the Latin rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: A monarch caught in the grip of one of the deadly sins, namely greed.
explanation.walkthrough: AR goes inside VICE to give VARICE, after the second 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Poems composed in the town of Derby

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Verses written in a provincial English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' suggests the city of that name; it is the horse race, run at Epsom in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is a famous flat horse race run each year on the Downs at this Surrey town.

clue.text: Expression of shock as king interrupts us

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into the middle of the word for us

parts.note: us is you and I, so the letters I and YOU
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch cuts in on our conversation, causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' means you and I, split so that the two pieces after it in the clue sit in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is an indignant cry of disbelief, like 'honestly!' or 'really!'.

clue.text: T. S. Eliot complicated? That's an understatement

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling the poet T. S. Eliot complicated is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'That's an understatement' reads as a quip, but 'understatement' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad', a form of deliberate understatement.

clue.text: Marine mollusc sailor single-handedly gathered

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
doing something single-handedly is doing it alone

explanation.surface: A seafarer collects shellfish by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' is a link at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: See, in his art, beginning of modernism perhaps

definitions.text: See, in his art, beginning of modernism perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps implies one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are rearranged
beginning of means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An invitation to view the work of a painter as the start of modernism.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEINHISART plus M, the first letter of 'modernism', rearrange to give the French painter, while the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Matisse, leader of the Fauves, is widely seen as a founding figure of modern painting.
